Attribute grazing water with an explicit accounting basis.

Source: R/grazing_water.R
calculate_grazing_water.Rd

Calculate water attributed to grazing from supplied evapotranspiration and biomass or valuation inputs. This calculator preserves the input's spatial and temporal context; it does not infer a reporting territory or annualize a study period. It does not download data or choose missing parameters.

biomass_allocation multiplies occupied-domain ET by consumed dry matter divided by reference available dry matter. Heinke et al. (2020), doi:10.1029/2019WR026995, Methods p. 3, use this attribution principle with ET and maximum biomass yield from dedicated grazing-intensity simulations. This function does not turn whole-plant NPP or realized herd intake into that reference yield. The caller must identify the reference basis and distinguish sourced estimates from explicit unverified assumptions. Reference ET and biomass must describe the same management scenario: ET from an actual stocking-rate run cannot silently be paired with a biomass maximum from a different experiment.

occupation attributes all supplied grassland ET to occupation of that domain. value_allocation applies a supplied economic allocation fraction to the same domain. Schyns et al. (2019), doi:10.1073/pnas.1817380116, Supplement S3, describe economic attribution; this function applies the supplied fraction and does not derive or validate its ecosystem valuation. These methods answer different accounting questions. None is a silent fallback for unavailable inputs to another method.

Usage

calculate_grazing_water(
  data,
  method = c("biomass_allocation", "occupation", "value_allocation"),
  excess = c("abort", "extrapolate")
)

Arguments

data

A tibble with component ("green" or "blue"), grass_water_m3 (ET over the reference grassland domain), and source_water. Biomass attribution also requires grass_intake_dm_t, reference_dm_t, source_intake, source_reference, reference_basis and reference_status ("sourced" or "assumed_unverified"). Matching water_scenario and reference_scenario labels identify the common reference experiment. An assumed reference requires a nonempty reference_assumption description. Economic attribution requires value_fraction between zero and one and source_fraction. Quantities must share the same domain and period. Source labels record provenance assertions; they are not verification. The input must not already contain this function's output columns.

method

Attribution method. The default "biomass_allocation" requires the supplied biomass reference. Alternatives are "occupation" and "value_allocation".

excess

Policy when intake exceeds reference biomass. "abort" (default) requires reconciliation of the inputs. "extrapolate" warns, preserves all intake, and reports an intensity-based water requirement which can exceed supplied ET. Such rows are not a physical ET partition.

Value

The input tibble with allocation_fraction, water_attributed_m3, water_unallocated_m3, excess_intake_dm_t, quantity_basis and method_grazing_water. Extrapolated excess rows have unknown unallocated water, recorded as NA, rather than a negative physical remainder. Non-biomass methods leave excess intake unknown. A declared zero intake and zero reference allocates zero water; positive intake against zero reference aborts under either policy. Green and blue rows can repeat the same intake/reference context. Do not sum those repeated biomass quantities across water components as separate feed. Compare methods by reusing the original inputs, not these results.

Examples

# Illustrative input, not a scientific coefficient or reference value.
data <- tibble::tribble(
  ~component, ~grass_water_m3, ~source_water,
  "green",    1000,            "Illustrative ET fixture"
)
calculate_grazing_water(data, method = "occupation")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   component grass_water_m3 source_water   allocation_fraction excess_intake_dm_t
#>   <chr>              <dbl> <chr>                        <dbl>              <dbl>
#> 1 green               1000 Illustrative …                   1                 NA
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: water_attributed_m3 <dbl>, water_unallocated_m3 <dbl>,
#> #   quantity_basis <chr>, method_grazing_water <chr>
